chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

If you forget a prayer or pray it without ablution, and there are missed prayers upon you, then begin with the first of them, call the Adhan for it and perform the Iqamah, then pray it, then pray what comes after it with an Iqamah, an Iqamah for each prayer.

And he (peace be upon him) said: And if you have prayed Dhuhr and the morning prayer has been missed by you, and you remember it, then pray the morning prayer whenever you remember it, even if it is after Asr; and whenever you remember a prayer that has been missed by you, pray it.

And he (peace be upon him) said: If you forget Dhuhr until you have prayed Asr, and you remember it while you are in the prayer or after its completion, intend it as the first, then pray Asr, for it is four [rak'at] in place of four [rak'at]. If you remember that you did not pray the first [Dhuhr] and you are in the prayer of Asr, and you have prayed two rak'at from it, intend it as the first, then pray the two remaining rak'at, and stand and pray Asr.

And if you remember that you did not pray Asr until the time for Maghrib enters, and you do not fear missing it, then pray Asr, then pray Maghrib. And if you have already prayed Maghrib, stand and pray Asr. And if you have prayed two rak'at from Maghrib, then you remember Asr, intend it as Asr, then stand and complete it with two rak'at, then give the Salam, then pray Maghrib.

So if you have prayed the last Isha and forgotten Maghrib, stand and pray Maghrib. And if you remembered it and you have prayed two rak'at from the last Isha, or you are standing in the third [rak'at], intend it as Maghrib, then give the Salam, then stand and pray the last Isha.

And if you have forgotten the last Isha until you have prayed Fajr, then pray the last Isha. And if you remember it while you are in the first rak'at or in the second of the morning [prayer], intend it as Isha, then stand and pray the morning [prayer], and call the Adhan and perform the Iqamah.

And if Maghrib and the last Isha have been missed by you together, begin with them before you pray the morning [prayer]. Begin with Maghrib, then the last Isha. If you fear that the morning prayer will be missed if you begin with them, then begin with Maghrib, then with the morning, then pray Isha. If you fear that the morning prayer will be missed if you begin with Maghrib, then pray the morning prayer, then pray Maghrib and Isha. Begin with the first of them, because they are both missed [prayers]; whichever of the two you remember, do not pray them except after the rays of the sun.
I said, 'Why is that?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'Because you are not fearing its being missed.'

key_terms.أَوَّلِهِنَّ: The first of them (referring to the earliest missed prayer)
key_terms.شُعَاعِ الشَّمْسِ: Rays of the sun (time for Dhuhr)
key_terms.فَوْتَهَا: Missing it (failing to pray within its time)

ai.seo_question: What is the procedure for making up missed prayers if you forget them or pray them without wudu?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* from Imam al-Baqir (AS), this hadith provides a comprehensive jurisprudential framework for *Qada* (making up) missed prayers, emphasizing the principle of sequential order (*tartib*) while allowing flexibility for *ikhtiyari* (voluntary) missed prayers. It details specific scenarios for overlapping prayers and the requirement of Adhan and Iqamah for each individual missed prayer, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preserving the distinct identity of each obligatory act. The ruling that one need not fear missing the time of *Qada* prayers underscores the divine mercy in accommodating human forgetfulness and sleep.
